chunks: And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام said: “Shall I not tell you about the will of Fāṭimah عليها السلام?” I said: “Yes.”

Then he brought out a box or a basket, and took out from it a document and read it: “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. This is what Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed. She bequeathed her seven orchards: al-‘Awāf, al-Dalāl, al-Burqah, al-Mīthab, al-Ḥusnā, al-Ṣāfiyah, and the property of Umm Ibrāhīm to ‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام. If ‘Alī passes away, then to al-Ḥasan; if al-Ḥasan passes away, then to al-Ḥusayn; and if al-Ḥusayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children. Allah is witness over that, and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad al-Kindī and al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwām.”
And it was written by: “‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام.”

key_terms.بِحَوَائِطِهَا: regarding her enclosed gardens or orchards

ai.seo_question: What does the will of Fāṭimah عليها السلام say about her property and its succession?
ai.summary: This narration records the written وصيّة of Fāṭimah عليها السلام regarding her properties and their succession after her. It highlights both the legal transfer of her estates and the ordered designation of authority within her household, with named witnesses and ‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام as the scribe.
